title: Late Breaking Results: A Fast Nearest Neighbor Search Acceleration for 3D Point Cloud
problem: K-Nearest Neighbors search in point clouds requires expensive Euclidean distance calculations over large candidate sets, limiting throughput on edge devices and real-time applications.
motivation: Point cloud processing is critical for autonomous systems and 3D vision; efficient KNN search is a fundamental bottleneck limiting edge deployment.
method: Uses locality-sensitive E2LSH partitioning to pre-filter candidate points, employs a precomparator module to reduce candidate search space further, and optimizes Euclidean distance computation to minimize expensive calculations while maintaining high precision.
key_novelty: Combination of locality-sensitive hashing (E2LSH) partitioning with precomparator filtering to significantly reduce candidate set while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: E2LSH-based partitioning method for candidate pre-filtering in KNN search
Precomparator module reducing candidate evaluation by 58.57%-86.17% vs. octree methods
10.04× throughput acceleration vs. BitNN comparator subsystem
FPGA-optimized architecture with improved resource utilization and precision
limitations: Limited to FPGA evaluation; scalability to very large point clouds (>1M points) not discussed.
primary_theme: FPGA KNN accelerator for point clouds via E2LSH partitioning and precomparator filtering
